newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwandan tribunal postpones trial to October 31.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan tribunal postpones trial to October 31.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda on Friday postponed the trial of a Rwandan Hutu accused of genocide and crimes against humanity to October 31 because the defence said it was not ready.

Presiding justice Yacov Ostrovsky, head of the three-judge panel, originally ruled that the trial of Jean Paul Akayesu should resume on Monday but later gave in after Belgian defence lawyer Johan Scheers objected.

Tribunal officials in Arusha also confirmed that a man they could not name had been arrested in Texas in the United States for taking part in the Rwandan genocide, which started in April 1994 after the murder of Hutu President Juvenal Habyarimana.
It was the second postponement ordered by the tribunal in three days. On Wednesday, the court delayed the trial of another Rwandan Hutu, Georges Rutaganda, to March next year.
"Our decision is...to resume the session at the last day of October, that is October 31," said the judge after the court refused to rule on a defence motion for Akayesu's temporary release.
The court also decided on Friday that witnesses in Akayesu's trial should not be identified to the public or media for their protection.
On Thursday, Scheers had threatened to resign unless the tribunal granted a postponement. He had also sought the temporary release of Akayesu.

Akayesu was the local government leader in Rwanda's Taba commune in the three-month genocide and is charged with failing to stop killings, inciting the public to slaughter, hunting down minority Tutsis and ordering killings.
The tribunal has been dogged by delays, poor communications from its base in the northern Tanzanian farming town of Arusha, and the vast problem of finding who was responsible for the genocide.
It has indicted only 21 suspects and has only three in detention, charged with crimes against humanity and genocide.
